records.source: אֵל־נְקָמ֥וֹת יְהוָ֑ה אֵ֖ל נְקָמ֣וֹת הוֹפִֽיַע׃
records.gloss: God of vengeance, YHWH, God of vengeance, shine forth!
pieces: God of retribution, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q God of retribution, shine out!

L.1: God of vengeance, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q God of vengeance, shine forth!

R.1: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the God who pays back evildoers. \q Show {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} in all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} brightness!

decisions.choice: vengeance: just punishment by the judge
decisions.reason: The word (neqamah) is not private revenge but the judge's act of setting wrong right (Deuteronomy 32:35, 41; Romans 12:19). God is asked to do what the judges of the land have failed to do (verses 20-21).

decisions.choice: shine forth: appear in glory
decisions.reason: The verb (yafa', causative) is used of God appearing to act (50:2; 80:2; Deuteronomy 33:2).

decisions.choice: a psalm for the fourth day
decisions.reason: Psalm 94 has no title in the Hebrew. The Mishnah (Tamid 7:4) lists it as the psalm sung in the temple on the fourth day of the week, and the ancient Greek translation gives it a title for that day.

decisions.choice: retribution (B); pays back evildoers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid a word that can suggest personal spite (m1).

records.heading: God who judges the earth, rise up

records.source: הִ֭נָּשֵׂא שֹׁפֵ֣ט הָאָ֑רֶץ הָשֵׁ֥ב גְּ֝מ֗וּל עַל־גֵּאִֽים׃
records.gloss: Lift yourself up, Judge of the earth; return recompense upon [the] proud.
pieces: Stand up, Judge of all the earth, \q and give the arrogant what their deeds have earned.

L.2: Lift {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} up, Judge of the earth; \q return recompense upon [the] proud.

R.2: Judge of the whole world, get up! \q Give proud people the punishment they deserve.

decisions.choice: Judge of the earth: Genesis 18:25
decisions.reason: Abraham called God "the Judge of all the earth" who will do what is right (Genesis 18:25).

decisions.choice: recompense: what one's deeds deserve
decisions.reason: The word (gemul) is a deed and what it earns in return (28:4).

records.source: עַד־מָתַ֖י רְשָׁעִ֥ים׀יְהוָ֑ה עַד־מָ֝תַ֗י רְשָׁעִ֥ים יַעֲלֹֽזוּ׃
records.gloss: Until when [will the] wicked, YHWH, until when will [the] wicked exult?
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, how much longer will the wicked, \q how much longer will the wicked celebrate?

L.3: How long [will the] wicked, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, \q how long will [the] wicked exult?

R.3: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, how long will wicked people keep on celebrating? \q How long?

decisions.choice: the repeated question
decisions.reason: The question breaks off and starts again, a pattern of Hebrew poetry (92:10; 93:3). "How long" is the cry of 13:2-3.

decisions.choice: exult: celebrate in triumph
decisions.reason: The verb ('alaz) is to rejoice loudly, here in their success.

records.source: יַבִּ֣יעוּ יְדַבְּר֣וּ עָתָ֑ק יִֽ֝תְאַמְּר֗וּ כָּל־פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: They pour forth, they speak arrogance; they boast, all [the] doers of wickedness.
pieces: Insolent words gush from them; \q everyone who does evil talks big.

L.4: They pour forth, they speak arrogant [words]; \q all who do wickedness boast.

R.4: They keep bragging and saying proud things. \q All these evil people boast about themselves.

decisions.choice: arrogance: insolent, proud speech
decisions.reason: The word ('ataq) is speech that is bold and contemptuous (31:19; 75:6).

decisions.choice: pour forth: gush like a spring
decisions.reason: The verb (nava') is used of a spring bubbling up (Proverbs 18:4): their boasting never stops.

records.source: עַמְּךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה יְדַכְּא֑וּ וְֽנַחֲלָתְךָ֥ יְעַנּֽוּ׃
records.gloss: Your people, YHWH, they crush, and your inheritance they afflict.
pieces: They grind down {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; \q they oppress the nation that belongs to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.5: Your people, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, they crush, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance they afflict.

R.5: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, they crush {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. \q They hurt the people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: your inheritance: the people who are God's own
decisions.reason: Israel is the LORD's inheritance, his own possession (28:9; 33:12; Deuteronomy 32:9).

decisions.choice: the nation (people) that belongs to you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the inheritance is (m1).

records.source: אַ֭לְמָנָה וְגֵ֣ר יַהֲרֹ֑גוּ וִֽיתוֹמִ֣ים יְרַצֵּֽחוּ׃
records.gloss: Widow and sojourner they kill, and fatherless [ones] they murder.
pieces: Widows and foreigners they put to death; \q orphans they murder.

L.6: [The] widow and [the] sojourner they kill, \q and [the] fatherless they murder.

R.6: They kill widows and foreigners who live among us. \q They murder children who have no father to protect them.

decisions.choice: widow, foreigner, orphan: the defenseless
decisions.reason: These three had no family or land to protect them, and the law puts them under God's care (Deuteronomy 10:18; 24:17; 27:19). To attack them is to defy God himself.

decisions.choice: sojourner: a foreigner living in the land
decisions.reason: The word (ger) is someone from elsewhere settled among Israel without the rights of a native.

decisions.choice: who live among us; to protect them
decisions.reason: Readable says who the foreigners and the fatherless are (m1, m2).

records.source: וַ֭יֹּ֣אמְרוּ לֹ֣א יִרְאֶה־יָּ֑הּ וְלֹא־יָ֝בִ֗ין אֱלֹהֵ֥י יַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: And they said, Not will see Yah, and not will perceive [the] God of Jacob.
pieces: They say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} is not looking; \q Jacob's God pays no attention."

L.7: And they say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} will not see, \q and the God of Jacob will not perceive."

R.7: They say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yah}} cannot see what we are doing. \q Israel's God does not even notice."

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a short form of the name YHWH, used mostly in poetry and in praise (Exodus 15:2; 68:5), and in the cry "Hallelu-yah". It names the same God; the divine name setting shows it as "the LORD" or "Yah".

decisions.choice: they said: what they keep saying
decisions.reason: The past form introduces what the wicked say and go on saying (10:11), so it is rendered in the present.

decisions.choice: the God of Jacob: Israel's own God
decisions.reason: Jacob is Israel (Genesis 32), so the wicked deny that the God of their own people sees what they do.

decisions.choice: Israel's God
decisions.reason: Readable uses the better-known name of the people (m3).

records.source: בִּ֭ינוּ בֹּעֲרִ֣ים בָּעָ֑ם וּ֝כְסִילִ֗ים מָתַ֥י תַּשְׂכִּֽילוּ׃
records.gloss: Understand, stupid [ones] among the people, and fools, when will you be wise?
pieces: Get some understanding, you brutish people! \q Fools, when will you start to think wisely?

L.8: Understand, [you] senseless among the people! \q And fools, when will you be wise?

R.8: You foolish people, think about this! \q When will you ever learn?

decisions.choice: stupid: dull as an animal
decisions.reason: The word (ba'ar) is the one of 92:7 and 73:22.

decisions.choice: among the people: within Israel
decisions.reason: The psalm now speaks to people within God's own people, the wicked of verses 4-7 or any who think as they do.

records.source: הֲנֹ֣טַֽע אֹ֭זֶןהֲלֹ֣א יִשְׁמָ֑ע אִֽם־יֹ֥צֵֽר עַ֝֗יִן הֲלֹ֣א יַבִּֽיט׃
records.gloss: The planter of [the] ear, does he not hear? Or [the] one who formed [the] eye, does he not see?
pieces: Will the one who set the ear in place not hear? \q Will the one who shaped the eye not see?

L.9: The one who planted the ear, does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not hear? \q Or the one who formed the eye, does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not see?

R.9: God made our ears. Of course {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can hear! \q He made our eyes. Of course {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} can see!

decisions.choice: planted, formed: made the body
decisions.reason: The ear is pictured as planted in the head; "formed" (yatsar) is the potter's verb used for the making of the first man (Genesis 2:7).

decisions.choice: questions that expect yes
decisions.reason: The answer to "Yah does not see" (verse 7): the maker of eyes sees.

decisions.choice: God; Of course
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions into statements and names God.

records.source: הֲיֹסֵ֣ר גּ֭וֹיִם הֲלֹ֣א יוֹכִ֑יחַ הַֽמְלַמֵּ֖ד אָדָ֣ם דָּֽעַת׃
records.gloss: The one who disciplines nations, does he not rebuke? — the one who teaches humankind knowledge.
pieces: Will the one who disciplines nations not correct them, \q the one who teaches humans all they know?

L.10: The one who disciplines nations, does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not rebuke — \q the one who teaches {{gender:humankind|man}} knowledge?

R.10: God corrects the nations. Of course {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will punish wicked people! \q He teaches people everything they know.

decisions.choice: the one who teaches: a line left open
alternatives: does the one who teaches knowledge not know?
decisions.reason: The last line has no verb of its own. It may describe the same God ("the one who teaches humankind knowledge") or imply a third question, "does he not know?", which verse 11 answers.

decisions.choice: disciplines, rebukes: corrects and punishes
decisions.reason: The verbs (yasar, yakach) are used of correction by a father or a judge (6:2; Proverbs 3:11-12).

decisions.choice: humankind (with "man" as the alternative at Literal); humans, people
decisions.reason: The word ('adam) means human beings, so Literal gives inclusive wording by default.

decisions.choice: punish wicked people
decisions.reason: Readable says whom God will correct.

records.source: יְֽהוָ֗ה יֹ֭דֵעַ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת אָדָ֑ם כִּי־הֵ֥מָּה הָֽבֶל׃
records.gloss: YHWH knows [the] thoughts of humankind, that they [are] a breath.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} knows what humans are thinking, \q and that their thoughts are only a puff of air.

L.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} knows the thoughts of {{gender:humankind|man}}, \q that they [are] a breath.

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} knows what people are thinking. \q He knows their thoughts are worthless, like a breath of air.

decisions.choice: a breath: empty, passing
decisions.reason: The word (hevel) is breath or vapor, something without substance (39:6; Ecclesiastes 1:2).

decisions.choice: they: the thoughts, or the people
decisions.reason: "They" may be the thoughts or the humans who think them; either way nothing of it lasts.

decisions.choice: quoted in 1 Corinthians 3:20
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the verse from the Greek translation as "the Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are futile".

decisions.choice: humankind (with "man" as the alternative at Literal); humans, people
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, the word ('adam) means human beings.

records.source: אַשְׁרֵ֤י׀הַגֶּ֣בֶר אֲשֶׁר־תְּיַסְּרֶ֣נּוּ יָּ֑הּ וּֽמִתּוֹרָתְךָ֥ תְלַמְּדֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: How blessed [is] the man whom you discipline, Yah, and from your instruction you teach him,
pieces: How blessed is {{gender:the one|the man}} whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} correct, {{divine_name:LORD|Yah}}, \q and train through {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction,

L.12: How blessed [is] {{gender:the one|the man}} whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} discipline, {{divine_name:LORD|Yah}}, \q and whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction,

R.12: {{divine_name:LORD|Yah}}, life is truly good for the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} correct \q and guide by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} teaching.

decisions.choice: How blessed: a life that goes well
decisions.reason: The exclamation ('ashre) of 1:1. The one God trains is better off than the wicked who seem to prosper.

decisions.choice: discipline: train and correct like a father
decisions.reason: The verb (yasar) of verse 10: as a father trains his son (Deuteronomy 8:5; Proverbs 3:11-12), God corrects his people, not to destroy them.

decisions.choice: Yah: the short form of the divine name
decisions.reason: Yah is a short form of the name YHWH, used mostly in poetry and in praise (Exodus 15:2; 68:5), and in the cry "Hallelu-yah". It names the same God; the divine name setting shows it as "the LORD" or "Yah".

decisions.choice: instruction: torah
decisions.reason: The word (torah) is God's teaching and direction for life (1:2).

decisions.choice: the one (with "the man" as the alternative); the people (R)
decisions.reason: The word (gever) is a man, but the blessing is for anyone God trains (1:1), so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default; Readable uses the plural.

decisions.choice: life is truly good for
decisions.reason: As in 1:1.

records.source: לְהַשְׁקִ֣יט ל֭וֹמִ֣ימֵי רָ֑ע עַ֤ד יִכָּרֶ֖ה לָרָשָׁ֣ע שָֽׁחַת׃
records.gloss: to give rest to him from days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked.
pieces: giving {{gender:them|him}} calm in the days of trouble, \q while the pit is being dug for the wicked.

L.13: to give {{gender:them|him}} rest from days of trouble, \q until a pit is dug for the wicked.

R.13: You give them peace when times are hard, \q until a grave is dug for wicked people.

decisions.choice: give rest: give quiet, calm
decisions.reason: The verb (shaqat) is to be quiet and undisturbed. God's teaching gives inner calm through the bad days, while the end of the wicked is being prepared.

decisions.choice: a pit is dug: their downfall is being prepared
decisions.reason: A pit is a trap or a grave (7:16; 9:16). The wicked who dug pits for others fall into one.

decisions.choice: a grave
decisions.reason: Readable gives one likely sense of the picture (m2).

records.source: כִּ֤י׀לֹא־יִטֹּ֣שׁ יְהוָ֣ה עַמּ֑וֹ וְ֝נַחֲלָת֗וֹ לֹ֣א יַעֲזֹֽב׃
records.gloss: For YHWH will not abandon his people, and his inheritance he will not forsake.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not reject {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will never desert those who belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.14: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not abandon {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not forsake.

R.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will never leave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people alone. \q He will not give up on the people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the LORD will not abandon his people: 1 Samuel 12:22
decisions.reason: Samuel promised the same with the same verb: "the LORD will not abandon his people, for the sake of his great name".

decisions.choice: his inheritance: his own people
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

records.source: כִּֽי־עַד־צֶ֭דֶק יָשׁ֣וּב מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וְ֝אַחֲרָ֗יו כָּל־יִשְׁרֵי־לֵֽב׃
records.gloss: For to righteousness judgment will return, and after it [will be] all [the] upright of heart.
pieces: For justice will once again be joined to what is right, \q and all who are honest at heart will follow it.

L.15: For judgment will return to righteousness, \q and after it [will go] all the upright of heart.

R.15: Once more, judging will be fair and right, \q and all honest people will follow that way.

decisions.choice: judgment: the giving of verdicts, justice
decisions.reason: The word (mishpat) is what judges do. Now it is twisted (verses 20-21); it will again be done rightly.

decisions.choice: judgment will return to righteousness: justice will be righteous again
alternatives: justice will return to the righteous
decisions.reason: The line says that judging will come back to what is right. Some read it as justice returning to the righteous person.

decisions.choice: upright of heart: people honest within
decisions.reason: As in 7:11 and 32:11.

records.source: מִֽי־יָק֣וּם לִ֭י עִם־מְרֵעִ֑ים מִֽי־יִתְיַצֵּ֥ב לִ֝י עִם־פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
records.gloss: Who will rise up for me against evildoers? Who will take his stand for me against doers of wickedness?
pieces: Who will take my side against the wicked? \q Who will stand with me against those who do wrong?

L.16: Who will rise up for me against evildoers? \q Who will take a stand for me against those who do wickedness?

R.16: Who will help me fight against evil people? \q Who will defend me against those who do wrong?

decisions.choice: who will rise up?: no human helper
decisions.reason: The questions find no one among people; verse 17 gives the answer: the LORD.

decisions.choice: rise up, take a stand: as a witness or defender in court
decisions.reason: The verbs are used of standing up in court for someone (Deuteronomy 19:16; Job 33:5).

records.source: לוּלֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה עֶזְרָ֣תָה לִּ֑י כִּמְעַ֓ט׀שָֽׁכְנָ֖ה דוּמָ֣ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: If YHWH [had] not [been] a help to me, soon my soul would have dwelt [in] silence.
pieces: If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not helped me, \q I would soon have been living where all is silent.

L.17: If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [had] not [been] a help to me, \q my soul would soon have dwelt [in] silence.

R.17: If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not helped me, \q I would soon have died and gone to the silent place of the dead.

decisions.choice: silence: the realm of the dead
decisions.reason: The word (dumah) is the silence of the grave, where no one praises God (115:17).

decisions.choice: my soul: I, my life
decisions.reason: The soul (nefesh) is the whole living person (6:4).

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "I" for "my soul" (m2).

decisions.choice: the silent place of the dead
decisions.reason: Readable says what the silence is (m1).

records.source: אִם־אָ֭מַרְתִּי מָ֣טָה רַגְלִ֑י חַסְדְּךָ֥ יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִסְעָדֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: When I said, My foot slips, your loyal love, YHWH, supported me.
pieces: The moment I said, "My foot is giving way," \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, held me up.

L.18: When I said, "My foot has slipped," \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, held me up.

R.18: When I cried, "I am falling!" \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love held me up, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: my foot slips: I am about to fall into disaster
decisions.reason: A slipping foot is a picture of coming to ruin (38:17; 73:2).

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: בְּרֹ֣ב שַׂרְעַפַּ֣י בְּקִרְבִּ֑י תַּ֝נְחוּמֶ֗יךָ יְֽשַׁעַשְׁע֥וּ נַפְשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: In [the] multitude of my anxious thoughts within me, your consolations delight my soul.
pieces: When my worries crowd in on me, \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} comfort fills me with joy.

L.19: In the multitude of my anxious thoughts within me, \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} consolations delight my soul.

R.19: When I am very worried, \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} comfort me and make me happy again.

decisions.choice: anxious thoughts: troubling, divided thoughts
decisions.reason: The word (sar'appim) is used of restless, worried thoughts (139:23).

decisions.choice: my soul: me
decisions.reason: As in verse 17: the whole person.

decisions.choice: me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "me" for "my soul" (m2).

records.source: הַֽ֭יְחָבְרְךָ כִּסֵּ֣א הַוּ֑וֹת יֹצֵ֖ר עָמָ֣ל עֲלֵי־חֹֽק׃
records.gloss: Can [the] throne of destruction be allied with you, [one that] frames mischief by statute?
pieces: Will a ruling power bent on ruin ever be {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} partner, \q one that uses the law to create misery?

L.20: Can a throne of destruction be allied with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q one that frames mischief by statute?

R.20: Can evil rulers be friends with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? \q They make laws that hurt people!

decisions.choice: a throne of destruction: corrupt rulers and courts
decisions.reason: A throne stands for those who rule and judge. Here they use their power and the law itself to harm the innocent (verse 21; Isaiah 10:1-2).

decisions.choice: frames: shapes, as a potter does
decisions.reason: The verb (yatsar) is the one used of God forming the eye (verse 9): God forms eyes to see, these rulers form misery.

decisions.choice: by statute: through the law
decisions.reason: The words ('ale-choq) most likely mean that they make harm into law; they could mean they plan trouble against what the law says.

records.source: יָ֭גוֹדּוּ עַל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ צַדִּ֑יק וְדָ֖ם נָקִ֣י יַרְשִֽׁיעוּ׃
records.gloss: They band together against [the] life of [the] righteous, and innocent blood they condemn.
pieces: They gather against the righteous to take their lives, \q and they condemn innocent people to death.

L.21: They band together against the life of the righteous, \q and innocent blood they condemn.

R.21: They plot together to kill people who do what is right. \q They sentence innocent people to death.

decisions.choice: innocent blood: an innocent person's life
decisions.reason: To condemn innocent blood is to sentence an innocent person to death (Deuteronomy 19:10; 27:25).

decisions.choice: band together: gather as a troop
decisions.reason: The verb (gadad) is related to a word for a band of raiders; it may mean they gather against or that they attack.

records.source: וַיְהִ֬י יְהוָ֣ה לִ֣י לְמִשְׂגָּ֑ב וֵ֝אלֹהַ֗י לְצ֣וּר מַחְסִֽי׃
records.gloss: But YHWH has become for me a high fortress, and my God [the] rock of my refuge.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has proved to be my high fortress; \q my God has been a rock that shelters me.

L.22: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has become for me a high fortress, \q and my God the rock of my refuge.

R.22: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keeps me safe like a strong fortress. \q My God is like a rock where I can run for safety.

decisions.choice: high fortress: a place out of reach
decisions.reason: The word (misgav) is a high, safe place (9:10; 18:3), from the verb of 91:14.

decisions.choice: refuge: shelter
decisions.reason: The word (machseh) is the one of 91:2 and 46:2.

records.source: וַיָּ֤שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֨ם׀אֶת־אוֹנָ֗ם וּבְרָעָתָ֥ם יַצְמִיתֵ֑ם יַ֝צְמִיתֵ֗ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And he has brought back on them their iniquity, and in their evil he will destroy them; YHWH our God will destroy them.
pieces: He will make their evil recoil on them \q and put an end to them through their own wickedness; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God will put an end to them.

L.23: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought back on them their iniquity, \q and in their evil {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy them; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God will destroy them.

R.23: God will punish them for the evil they have done. \q He will destroy them because they are wicked. \q Yes, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God will wipe them out.

decisions.choice: he has brought back: as good as done
decisions.reason: The first verb is in a past form; the next two are future. The psalmist speaks of God's judgment as already settled.

decisions.choice: bring back their iniquity on them: their evil comes back on them
decisions.reason: The wrong they did returns on their own heads (7:17).

decisions.choice: destroy: put an end to, silence
decisions.reason: The verb (tsamat) means to destroy completely, to silence (18:41; 54:7).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names who acts.
